card.summary: The Provider Reimbursement Stability Act of 2026 makes changes to how annual adjustments and payments are managed under the Medicare physician fee schedule. It raises the threshold for budget neutrality adjustments, requires corrections when actual service usage differs from estimated usage for certain bundled or separate services, mandates regular updates to direct cost inputs at least every five years, and places a limit on how much a conversion factor may vary from year to year.

summary: H.R. 9693, titled the Patients First Act of 2026, makes multiple changes to how physicians and health care practitioners are paid under the Medicare program. The bill creates a temporary hybrid payment model for certain primary care services, renames and restructures the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) into the Patient Outcome Improvement National Tabulation System (POINTS), adjusts how annual fee schedule updates and budget neutrality thresholds are calculated, and changes data collection and reporting requirements for imaging services and clinical data registries.

affected_groups.effect: Receive primary care under a hybrid payment model with no applicable cost sharing for those monthly payments, and experience updated quality and care efficiency metrics applied to their providers.
May opt into a monthly hybrid payment model for certain primary care services if owned or controlled by health care practitioners and meeting specific revenue thresholds.

Subject to restructured performance categories (including care efficiency), modified payment adjustments, new reporting incentives, and distinct rules if practicing in entities owned by non-practitioner entities.
Subject to new establishment and operational standards, three-year approval periods, and granted broader access to Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP claims data for research and quality improvement.

key_provisions: Establishes a temporary hybrid payment model for 2027 through 2031 where qualifying primary care practices receive monthly payments per attributed patient instead of individual fee-for-service payments for designated primary care services.
Renames the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) to the Patient Outcome Improvement National Tabulation System (POINTS) beginning in 2032 and adds care efficiency as a performance category.

Modifies annual conversion factor updates for Medicare physician services starting in 2027 to be based on estimated percentage increases in the Medicare Economic Index (MEI) with specific floors and ceilings.
Establishes a Quality Reform Task Force to issue recommendations on quality, resource use, and care efficiency measures for the POINTS program.
Adjusts the work geographic index during high inflationary years and changes budget neutrality thresholds, correction mechanisms for estimated utilization, and conversion factor variance limitations.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for national average monthly primary care hybrid payments before geographic and risk adjustments.
Specific details on the exact formulas the Secretary will use for risk adjustment and geographic indices in the hybrid model.
The precise numerical thresholds the Secretary will establish to designate 'low compliant ordering professionals' under appropriate use criteria for imaging services.

The bill creates a temporary hybrid payment model for certain primary care services, renames and restructures the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) into the Patient Outcome Improvement National Tabulation System (POINTS), adjusts how annual fee schedule updates and budget neutrality thresholds are calculated, and changes data collection and reporting requirements for imaging services and clinical data registries.
summary_detail.significance: The bill implements sweeping changes to Medicare physician payment structures, modifying how primary care is funded via hybrid models, altering the evaluation and scoring systems for provider performance, and revising federal rules governing payment updates and budget neutrality.
